Returns. Pulling together the numbers behind the VAT returns and the direct tax returns, applying the agreed treatment, and handing the Tax Manager a pack that's ready to review and file.
Reconciliations. Tying what's been reported back to the accounts, and keeping workings clear enough that a reviewer or auditor can follow them without asking you.
Tax accounting. Preparing the current and deferred tax numbers and disclosures, and flagging anything that's moved or looks unusual.
Reporting. Taking a share of the statutory and group submissions, along with the external statistical and regulatory returns.
Data. Getting what you need out of the ledger and other systems, checking it, and improving how it's sourced so nobody rebuilds it from scratch every period.
Projects. Helping with Pillar Two, transfer pricing and a finance system change, mainly by testing that the data and treatment come through correctly.
Why that matters
VAT specialists who also understand corporation tax, tax accounting and reporting are far rarer than either on their own. That breadth tends to open the doors that a single specialism keeps shut.
And you'd be building it on top of something you already know well, rather than starting again.

Someone part qualified
